# llms.txt — LingoFuse-Tools

> **Machine-readable index for AI agents and LLM crawlers.**
> This file tells an LLM what this repository does, which documents are authoritative, and in what order to read them.

---

## 1. What This Repository Is

**LingoFuse-Tools** is the **interface generation layer** of the [LingoFuse](https://github.com/PassByYou888/LingoFuse) cross-language communication foundation.

It solves one problem: **a cross-language interface is expensive to maintain, not expensive to write once.** One `Add(a, b: Integer): Integer` must exist in Python, C++, C#, Rust, Go, Java, JS, TS, Erlang, Julia, Zig, Swift, Ruby, Fortran, Dart, R — plus tests, build scripts, and docs. Change the signature once, and every language can silently drift out of alignment.

LingoFuse-Tools turns the interface from a **maintenance burden** into a **generated artifact**. You maintain **one declaration** (a Pascal unit or a C header). The toolchain projects it onto every target language, every protocol, every test and build script. Change the declaration, regenerate, all targets refresh together. **There is no hand-maintained per-language copy that can drift, because there is no hand-maintained per-language copy.**

**Three tools, three protocols, one input contract:**

| Tool | Protocol | Directory |
|------|----------|-----------|
| `code_decl_to_abi` | LingoFuse binary ABI | `src/pascal_c_to_abi/` |
| `code_decl_to_json_abi` | HTTP + JSON (via `bridge.py`) | `src/pascal_c_to_json_abi/` |
| `code_decl_to_mcp` | Model Context Protocol | `src/pascal_c_to_mcp/` |

**Every tool supports three entry points** — GUI, CLI, and MCP API — and **ships with a self-contained knowledge base** for full AI takeover. GUI/CLI/MCP outputs are byte-identical; MCP `internal_call_*` calls the same handlers the GUI uses.

---

## 2. The Three Tool Lines: How to Choose

| Scenario | Tool |
|---|---|
| Both ends can load the LingoFuse runtime; numeric/string-heavy payloads; high concurrency | `code_decl_to_abi` |
| One end is a browser, an external HTTP client, or a language with no LingoFuse binding | `code_decl_to_json_abi` |
| The function should become an MCP tool an AI agent can discover | `code_decl_to_mcp` |

**Language coverage (deduplicated):** 20 target languages. `code_decl_to_abi` covers 17 with both Service and Call. `code_decl_to_json_abi` covers 20 with both Service and Call, **except** JavaScript (browser), PHP, and Delphi which are **Call-only**. `code_decl_to_mcp` covers 4 (Pascal, Python, C++, C#).

**Delphi, PHP, and JavaScript (browser) appear only in the JSON line, and only on the Call side.** They have no Service generation and no ABI/MCP generator.

---

## 3. Authoritative Documents — Read in This Order

An LLM agent should read the following documents **in order**. Each document is written to be consumed without reading the tool's source code.

### Step 1 — Project-level overview

| Document | Path | Purpose |
|----------|------|---------|
| **README** | `README.md` | Repository purpose, three tools, three entry points, quick start, ecosystem |
| **Toolchain knowledge base** | `src/pascal_c_to_mcp/code_decl_to_mcp_knowledge_base.md` | Developer-facing KB for the MCP generator; covers all generators' shared logic |

### Step 2 — Tool-specific knowledge bases

Read the KB for the tool you intend to use.

| Tool | Knowledge base | User guide |
|------|----------------|------------|
| `code_decl_to_abi` | `src/pascal_c_to_abi/code_decl_to_abi_OPERATIONS.md` | `src/pascal_c_to_abi/code_decl_to_abi_USER_GUIDE.md` |
| `code_decl_to_json_abi` | `src/pascal_c_to_json_abi/code_decl_to_json_abi_knowledge_base.md` | `src/pascal_c_to_json_abi/code_decl_to_json_abi_USER_GUIDE.md` |
| `code_decl_to_mcp` | `src/pascal_c_to_mcp/code_decl_to_mcp_knowledge_base.md` | `src/pascal_c_to_mcp/code_generate_mcp.md` |

### Step 3 — Declaration rules (parsing contracts)

Before feeding a declaration to any tool, read the corresponding rule document. **These documents ARE the parsing contract** — anything that violates them is silently dropped.

| Source language | Rule document |
|-----------------|---------------|
| Pascal | `src/pascal_c_to_abi/pascal_code_abi_rule.md` |
| C | `src/pascal_c_to_abi/C_code_abi_rule.md` |
| MCP-specific contracts | `src/pascal_c_to_mcp/MCP_API_Contract.md` |

> **Silently dropped** means: not "partially generated", not "runtime error", but **the entire declaration is excluded during normalization**. The generator logs a reason; it does not emit a broken artifact.

### Step 4 — Tool description authoring (critical for agents)

| Document | Path | Purpose |
|----------|------|---------|
| **Writing Tool Descriptions for AI** | `src/pascal_c_to_mcp/code_generate_mcp.md` §10 | **THE MOST IMPORTANT CHAPTER.** Explains why AI agents stall on ambiguous tool descriptions and how to write descriptions that agents can act on. |

---

## 4. Canonical Q&A for Agents

### Q: What does this repository do?

A: It generates cross-language binding code. Give it a Pascal unit or C header; it produces service-side and caller-side code for multiple target languages, plus a companion Markdown README for every artifact.

### Q: What is the "single source of truth"?

A: `TPascal_Func_Model` (the LV1 intermediate model). Every generator — for every language, every protocol, every test — reads from this same model. Code and companion Markdown are generated in the same pass, so **they never drift out of sync**.

### Q: How do I drive a tool?

| Entry point | How |
|-------------|-----|
| **GUI** | Launch the executable with **no arguments**; drive the five tabs (Welcome → Source Code → Source ↔ JSON → JSON ↔ Model → Final Source) |
| **CLI** | Launch with **arguments**; source and target languages are detected from file extensions |
| **MCP API** | Register with the `agent_main_app` beacon; drive through MCP tool calls |
| **Programmatic** | Call `GenerateXxxCode(Model)` from your own Pascal unit; the generators are ordinary Pascal units |

### Q: What MCP tools does each tool expose?

| Tool | MCP tools | Notes |
|------|-----------|-------|
| `code_decl_to_abi` | 31 | Per-language Convert + Read, plus pipeline-level tools |
| `code_decl_to_json_abi` | 3 | `Generate` / `ListFiles` / `GetFile` — deliberate minimal surface |
| `code_decl_to_mcp` | 11 | `SetSourceCode` / `ConvertToXxxMCP` / `GetLastXxxCode` / `Readme` etc. |

**Three-step MCP workflow** (for `code_decl_to_mcp`): `SetSourceCode` → `ConvertToXxxMCP` → `GetLastXxxCode` / `Readme`. No GUI interaction, no CLI invocation, indistinguishable from calling any other MCP tool.

### Q: What types are supported?

Only three normalized type families. **Anything outside these three families causes the entire declaration to be silently dropped.**

- **Integer** — `integer`, `int64`, `cardinal`, `longint`, `dword`, `word`, `smallint`, `byte`, `uint64`, `longword`
- **Float** — `double`, `single`, `extended`, `real`
- **String** — `string`, `ansistring`, `unicodestring`, `tpascalstring`, `tupascalstring`, `tp_string`, `pchar`, `pansichar`, `pwidechar`

**Everything else causes the entire declaration to be silently dropped.** This includes `Boolean`, `Variant`, arrays, records, classes, interfaces, enums, sets, generics, pointers, function pointers, `Currency`, `Comp`, and `TDateTime`.

**Workaround**: serialize complex values into a JSON `string` and deserialize on the receiving side. This is the **only supported escape hatch** for complex types.

**Procedures (no return value)** are valid — they generate `void` return types in target languages. Only the parameter and return **types** are restricted, not the function/procedure distinction.

### Q: What are the known pitfalls?

The knowledge bases document all known pitfalls with stable IDs. See `LingoFuse_Pascal_Complete_Guide.md` (under `src/common/`) for the Pascal core-layer pitfalls:

| ID prefix | Subsystem |
|-----------|-----------|
| `LF-APP-*` | Application/handle layer |
| `LF-CB-*` | Callback layer |
| `LF-DATA-*` | Data handle layer |
| `LF-NET-*` | Network preparation |
| `LF-CALL-*` | Remote call |
| `LF-SEQ-*` | Sequenced notify |
| `LF-CHK-*` | Query/cache |
| `LF-OPT-*` | Runtime options |
| `LF-CLEAN-*` | Cleanup/lifecycle |
| `LF-THREAD-*` | Threading model |
| `LF-TYPE-*` | Types/compilation |
| `LF-XLANG-*` | Cross-language data |
| `LF-JSON-*` | JSON usage layer |

**The four iron rules** (from `LingoFuse_Pascal_Complete_Guide.md`):

1. Callbacks **must** be `cdecl`, and **must not** call blocking LingoFuse functions inside the callback.
2. Data handles **must** be explicitly freed with `LF_FreeData`; do not rely on the 5-minute auto-reclaim.
3. Cleanup order **must** be `LF_ExitMainThread` → `LF_FreeApp` → `LF_Shutdown`.
4. `TZ_JsonObject` is a tree. `Parae` / `Assign` / `LoadFromStream` / `ParseText` may only be called on the **root** object. Use `TZ_JsonString` for intermediate JSON assembly; call `.Bytes` only at the end.

### Q: What is the generated README for?

Every generated artifact is paired with a Markdown companion. **The README is the real deliverable.**

- It contains the **test program**, the **interface reference**, the **build instructions**, and — for C++ — the **CMake script**.
- Code and README are generated from the same `TPascal_Func_Model` in the same pass, so **they never drift out of sync**.
- **Read the generated `.md` first** whenever you are about to build, test, or deploy an artifact.

### Q: How do I add a new target language?

Adding a new target language is a **mechanical 8-step process** (see `code_decl_to_abi_OPERATIONS.md` Chapter 14):

1. Create `<lang>_abi_service_generator_tool.pas`.
2. Create `<lang>_abi_call_generator_tool.pas`.
3. Provide a type mapping table (integer / float / string → target language native types).
4. Register in `code_decl_to_abi.lpr` `uses`.
5. Register in `code_decl_to_abi_cmdline.pas` `uses`, `Detect_Target_Lang`, `Execute_Conversion`.
6. Register in `code_decl_to_abi_frm.pas` `uses`, `GenerateSourceButtonClick`.
7. Add GUI tab sheets and their `TSynEdit` controls to the `.lfm`.
8. Add Convert tools and Readers to the MCP provider; update the `regCount` assertion.

**The backend has no architectural ceiling.** Any language with (a) a C-ABI-compatible FFI, (b) a runtime that speaks LingoFuse's wire protocol, and (c) a way to marshal the three ABI families is a candidate.

### Q: How do I add a new MCP tool?

1. Declare `internal_call_*` in the `interface` section.
2. Implement it in `implementation` using the `TCompute.Sync` pattern.
3. Add an `LF_RegisterCallEx` in `RegisterAPIs`.
4. Add the `ToolDef` assembly + `RegisterTool(ToolDef)` call in `RegisterTools`.
5. Update the `regCount` assertion.

### Q: What is the wire protocol?

**ABI wire format** (from `code_decl_to_abi_OPERATIONS.md` Chapter 7.5):

```
Request  = [field1][field2]...[fieldN]
Response = [status:uint8_t][payload]
  status = 0x00 → payload = serialized result
  status = 0xFF → payload = UTF-8 error message
```

**HTTP/JSON wire format** (from `code_decl_to_json_abi_knowledge_base.md` Chapter 9):

```
Request  = {"args": [v1, v2, ...]}
Response = {"code": 0, "result": <value>}
           {"code": -1, "error": "<message>"}
           {"code": -2, "error": "<message>"}  # request shape error
           {"code": -3, "error": "<message>"}  # precheck failed
```

**MCP tool response format** (from `MCP_API_Contract.md` Chapter 6):

```
Function success : {"result": <value>}
Procedure success: {"status": "ok"}
Any error        : {"error": "<msg>"}
```

### Q: What are the CLI exit codes?

| Code | Meaning |
|:----:|---------|
| 0 | Conversion succeeded |
| 1 | Missing or invalid arguments |
| 2 | Source parsing failed |
| 3 | Code generation failed |
| 4 | File I/O error |

### Q: How do I start an end-to-end service/caller pair?

1. **Start the service** — run the compiled service executable.
2. **Start the bridge** (`code_decl_to_json_abi` only) — `python3 bridge.py --endpoint ipc:<Unit>_abi --port 8081 --no-precheck`.
3. **Start the caller** — run the compiled caller executable or open the HTML test page.

**The bridge must always be running** for any HTTP/JSON call artifact to work. The service itself does not go through the bridge.

### Q: What is the "no drift" guarantee?

All three tools generate **code, tests, build scripts, and companion Markdown from the same `TPascal_Func_Model` in the same pass**. There is no separate "interface definition" that can drift from "interface implementation". This is structurally different from gRPC's `.proto`-to-stub model: `.proto` is a **separate artifact**; `TPascal_Func_Model` is **derived directly from the implementation source**.


### `src/common/`

```
lf_http_bridge_client.pas        # HTTP bridge client for Pascal

LingoFuse_Pascal_Complete_Guide.md  # Pascal core layer pitfalls KB
```

### `src/pascal_c_to_abi/`

```
code_decl_to_abi.lpr             # Main program (GUI + CLI dispatch)
code_decl_to_abi_cmdline.pas     # CLI frontend
code_decl_to_abi_frm.pas / .lfm  # GUI frontend
code_decl_to_abi_mcp_api_tool_provider_unit.pas  # 31 MCP tools
<lang>_abi_service_generator_tool.pas   # <lang> = pas / py / cpp / csharp / rust / go / java / nodejs / ts / erlang / julia / zig / swift / ruby / fortran / dart / r
<lang>_abi_call_generator_tool.pas      # same <lang> set
<lang>_abi_test_generator_tool.pas      # per-language test program (where applicable)
cpp_abi_cmake_generator_tool.pas        # CMake + C++ test program
pascal_code_abi_rule.md          # Pascal declaration rule
C_code_abi_rule.md               # C declaration rule
code_decl_to_abi_OPERATIONS.md   # Developer knowledge base
code_decl_to_abi_USER_GUIDE.md   # End-to-end user guide
```

**Generator naming pattern**: every target language contributes `<lang>_abi_service_generator_tool.pas` and `<lang>_abi_call_generator_tool.pas`. The 17 `<lang>` values are: `pas`, `py`, `cpp`, `csharp`, `rust`, `go`, `java`, `nodejs`, `ts`, `erlang`, `julia`, `zig`, `swift`, `ruby`, `fortran`, `dart`, `r`.

### `src/pascal_c_to_json_abi/`

```
code_decl_to_json_abi.lpr        # Main program
code_decl_to_json_abi_cmdline.pas # CLI frontend
code_decl_to_abi_json_frm.pas / .lfm  # GUI frontend
code_decl_to_json_abi_mcp_api_tool_provider_unit.pas  # 3 MCP tools
http_<lang>_abi_service_generator_tool.pas   # same 17 <lang> as ABI line
http_<lang>_abi_call_generator_tool.pas      # same 17 <lang>
http_js_abi_call_generator_tool.pas          # JavaScript (browser) — Call only
http_cmake_generator_tool.pas                # CMake + C++ test driver
C_code_abi_rule.md               # C declaration rule
pascal_code_abi_rule.md          # Pascal declaration rule
code_decl_to_json_abi_knowledge_base.md  # Developer knowledge base
code_decl_to_json_abi_USER_GUIDE.md      # End-to-end user guide
```

**Note**: the JSON line additionally has `http_js_abi_call_generator_tool.pas` (Call-only) and `http_bridge_setup_generator_tool.pas` (bridge launch scripts). The 20 target languages are the 17 ABI languages + JavaScript (browser) + PHP + Delphi — but PHP and Delphi also appear in the ABI directory as `<lang>_abi_*` generators for Call-only generation.

### `src/pascal_c_to_mcp/`

```
code_decl_to_mcp.lpr             # Main program
code_decl_to_mcp_cmdline.pas     # CLI frontend

py_mcp_generator_tool.pas        # Python MCP generator
cpp_mcp_generator_tool.pas       # C++ MCP generator
csharp_mcp_generator_tool.pas    # C# MCP generator (delivered, not integrated)
cmake_for_cpp_mcp_generator_tool.pas  # CMake + C++ test generator
pascal_code_mcp_rule.md          # Pascal declaration rule for MCP
C_code_mcp_rule.md               # C declaration rule for MCP

pascal_agent_api_ref_json.md     # Tool registration JSON reference

```

### `src/zCore/`

Submodule providing `Z.Core`, `Z.Json`, `Z.Pascal_Func_Model`, `Z.Pascal_Func_Tool`, etc.

## 6. Glossary

| Term | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| **LV0** | Raw parser output — syntactic metadata (source positions, raw type spellings, modifiers) |
| **LV1** | Normalized model (`TPascal_Func_Model`) — the only intermediate that generators see |
| **`TPascal_Func_Model`** | The single source of truth for all code and documentation generation |
| **Beacon** | LingoFuse tool registry — agents discover available tools here (default `agent_main_app`) |
| **App name** | LingoFuse application identity; matches case-insensitively on the network |
| **Data handle** (`TDataHnd`) | Opaque byte buffer containing an API name and payload |
| **Sequenced Notify** | FIFO-ordered notification for a given `(App, API)` pair |
| **MCP** | Model Context Protocol — the agent-to-tool communication standard |
| **Bridge** | `bridge.py` — the HTTP↔RPC forwarder required by all HTTP/JSON call artifacts |
| **Companion Markdown** | The `.md` file generated alongside every code artifact; contains build/test/deploy instructions |
| **Companion Markdown is the real deliverable** | The generated `.md` contains the test program, interface reference, build instructions, and CMake script. Read it before building or deploying. |

## 7. Repository Metadata

- **Owner**: [PassByYou888](https://github.com/PassByYou888)
- **License**: MIT (consistent with the LingoFuse ecosystem)
- **Language**: English throughout (documents and generated artifacts)
- **Build system**: Lazarus / FPC (`lazbuild`) or Delphi
- **Cross-platform**: Windows, Linux, macOS (any platform with a UI subsystem)
- **Target languages (deduplicated)**: **20**
  - `code_decl_to_abi`: 17 (Service + Call)
  - `code_decl_to_json_abi`: 20 (Service + Call, except JS/PHP/Delphi Call-only)
  - `code_decl_to_mcp`: 4 (Pascal, Python, C++, C#)
- **Roadmap**: 30 target programming languages (mechanical 8-step extension process; no architectural ceiling)

---

## 9. What This Repository Is Not

- **Not a general-purpose code-generation framework.** It generates cross-language bindings for LingoFuse. It does not generate ORMs, REST clients, protobuf stubs, or anything unrelated to LingoFuse's wire protocol.
- **Not an IDL-first system.** There is no separate IDL. The declaration **is** the implementation. This is why there is no IDL-drift failure mode.
- **Not a "one command, all languages, no setup" tool.** The generators themselves must be built (FPC / Lazarus). Target-language build scripts require the target language's toolchain to be installed. The generator guarantees **the generated code is complete**; it does not guarantee **your machine has every compiler pre-installed**.
- **Not suitable for object-in / object-out interfaces.** Types outside the three ABI families are dropped. You must make a serialization decision at the declaration level. This is deliberate friction, not a defect.
- **Not a community-supported project.** Single maintainer. Issues are answered, but no SLA, no Stack Overflow, no third-party tutorials.
